title: NLTK NKJPCorpusReader -- T1005 builtin open() bypasses the pathsec sandbox even under ENFORCE mode
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-12072 (GHSA-6hm5-jgcp-p838,
CVSS 7.5 HIGH), affecting NLTK's `NKJPCorpusReader`.

NLTK's `SECURITY.md` promises that file access is validated against
allowed data directories and that `nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE = True`
raises `PermissionError` on unauthorized access -- a guarantee
enforced through `FileSystemPathPointer.open()` calling
`nltk.pathsec.validate_path()`. `NKJPCorpusReader` never routes
through that protected path: `add_root()` builds the file path by
plain string concatenation (`self.root + fileid`, no `..`
stripping), and both `NKJPCorpus_Header_View` and `XML_Tool` open the
resulting path with the builtin `open()` rather than
`PathPointer.open()` -- so `pathsec`'s sentinel is never invoked and
`ENFORCE = True` provides no protection at all. A `fileids` argument
containing `../` sequences reaches `header()`, `raw()`, `words()`,
`sents()`, or `tagged_words()` and returns the parsed content of a
file outside the corpus root to the caller.

Detection logic flags an `NKJPCorpusReader` read invocation whose
`fileids` argument contains a `../` path-traversal sequence -- the
exact escape this advisory's proof of concept uses to read a
secret-marked `header.xml` planted outside a legitimate, empty corpus
root.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (nltk, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact source file, line numbers for
`add_root()`/`XML_Tool`, and a runnable proof of concept with an
out-of-root secret marker), fixed in NLTK 3.10.0 (PR #3579, verified via live GitHub changelog lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
